name: Dab Grot (the Grot Oak)

location.address: Near ul. Podchorazych, Deblin, Lubelskie Voivodeship, Poland

verified_sources: http://web.archive.org/web/20210515105435/https://www.dziennikwschodni.pl/pulawy/deblin-dab-grot-drzewem-roku,n,1000132719.html (Dziennik Wschodni, 2011-07-05, fetched via Wayback Machine after the live URL 404'd)

https://lubiehrubie.pl/region/polski-pomnik-przyrody-deblinski-dab-jagielly-grot-uczestnikiem-konkursu-na-europejskie-drzewo-roku-2012/ (title only, live fetch 403'd; corroborates the 2012 European Tree of the Year entry independently)
https://www.geocaching.com/geocache/GC5JJVX_deblin-1-dab-grot (69 logged visits, weak supporting evidence it is a real, reachable, currently-existing destination)
access: Free, standing in the open near ul. Podchorazych in Deblin; a public geocache is placed at it with dozens of logged visits. The 2011 article describes plans for a protective fence and information plaque and a nearby cycle path to Pulawy; not independently confirmed whether these were built.
transport: Deblin, Lubelskie Voivodeship, near ul. Podchorazych.
verify_notes: FAME EVIDENCE, confirmed on a fetched primary source (Dziennik Wschodni, 2011-07-05, via Wayback Machine snapshot since the live URL 404s today): Grot won the FIRST-EVER Polish 'Drzewo Roku' (Tree of the Year) contest, organised by Klub Gaja in 2011 as the Polish leg of the international 'European Tree of the Year' project, beating Katowice's beech 'Anton' in the final public vote (nearly 3,500 votes for Grot in that final round, over 15,000 voters total across the whole contest, competing against 85 nominated monument trees from 12 voivodeships). Quoted from Jacek Bozek of Klub Gaja. It was nominated by students of Gimnazjum nr 2 in Deblin (teacher Jolanta Karas). A second, independently-titled source (lubiehrubie.pl, title only, live fetch blocked with HTTP 403) separately names it as Poland's entrant in the 2012 European Tree of the Year contest, consistent with winning the 2011 domestic contest. MEASUREMENTS, from the same fetched 2011 article, in the reporter's own words: 28 metres tall, 16 metre crown spread, 6 metre (600cm) trunk girth (obwod pnia). AGE, quoted directly and kept exactly as vague as the source states it: 'liczy sobie przynajmniej 500 lat' (at least 500 years old) -- recorded as age_estimate 'at least 500 years' with a broad open-ended band (500-650) rather than invented precision; this SUPERSEDES an earlier WebSearch AI-summary figure of '~350 years' which is now known to be wrong (the actual source says at least 500) and is a good example of why summary figures must be checked against the fetched page. LEGEND (from the same article): pressing your left hand to the trunk and whispering a wish is said to grant it. HISTORY: connected to the building of the Deblin fortress on the order of Tsar Nicholas I, during which many similar trees in the area were felled; described by the article as having witnessed wartime upheavals. A separate, unconfirmed claim (from a search summary only, not seen on the fetched article) is that the tree/oak grove was earlier called 'Dab Jagielly Grot' after one 'Grot of Jankowice' who held the Deblin estate from 1397; NOT used as a stated fact here since it wasn't found on any fetched page, only mentioned for a future pass to check. ALIVE: no death report found; the geocaching page's 69 logged visits over an extended period are indirect supporting evidence of continued standing presence, though undated individually. Location: coordinate taken as given in the brief and not independently re-verified against a primary source this pass (the two articles found describe the tree narratively rather than with coordinates), hence location_precision approximate; a future pass could tighten this via satellite imagery or a geotagged photo. New place, no published city nearby; ships under the 2026-08-31 single-famous-tree exception on strong, sourced contest-win fame (the clearest case in this whole batch).

name: The Kneeling Tree (Klekace Drzewo)

location.address: Rynek (market square), Krasnystaw, Lubelskie Voivodeship, Poland

verified_sources: https://50ok.pl/krasnystaw-kleczace-drzewo-na-rynku/ (2024, fetched directly, quotes the tree's own on-site interpretive plaque verbatim)
https://pl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnystaw#Zabytki (cited within the above source, describing the 2018 Drzewo Roku win)
https://lublin.tvp.pl/42024815/kleczace-drzewo-z-krasnegostawu-na-europejskiej-liscie (search result confirming it reached the European Tree of the Year shortlist)
access: Free. Stands in the open on Krasnystaw's town market square (Rynek), beside the town hall and a fountain; a public square, no permission needed.
transport: Central Krasnystaw, on the market square (Rynek).
verify_notes: FAME EVIDENCE, unusually strong and unusually well documented for its size/age (a genus/age combination that alone would not otherwise clear the bar; this ships on FAME rather than age or girth, per the species_size doctrine that the best of the three axes counts and per the explicit contest-win test in this batch's own brief). Confirmed on a fetched source (50ok.pl, a 2024 travel blog post) that quotes the tree's OWN on-site interpretive plaque directly: name 'klekace drzewo' (kneeling tree), species klon jesionolistny (Acer negundo, boxelder/ash-leaved maple), site Krasnystaw town market square, age approx. 65 years, height 9m, girth (obwod pnia) 182cm, distinguishing feature: a trunk grown near-horizontal to the ground (hence the name), coined from a poet's words per the plaque; locals also just call it 'the crooked/bent tree'. Nominated by the Krasnystaw Ecological Movement 'Viridis' for the 2018 national 'Drzewo Roku' (Tree of the Year) contest and WON with 4,131 public votes, beating (per the same plaque) Krakow's Dab Henryka, the Ustrobniak Oak (Podkarpackie) and a third, separate 'Dab Bartek' in Wielkopolskie voivodeship (yet another same-named oak, distinct from both the Zagnansk national-icon Bartek and the Bydgoszcz local Bartek checked earlier this same pass -- do not conflate any of the three). The win advanced it to the 2019 European Tree of the Year contest against 12 other European finalists; a search result (lublin.tvp.pl headline 'Kleczace drzewo z Krasnegostawu na europejskiej liscie') independently confirms it reached that European shortlist, and an earlier WebSearch summary (not independently fetched, treated as a lead only) reported it placed 6th. The tree also appears on a postal stamp in a small 'Krasnystaw' series and is treated locally as one of the town's civic symbols. ALIVE: the fetched source is from April 2024 with the author's own photograph from March 2024, recent and direct evidence of current standing presence. ACCESS: a public town market square, fully open, no restriction of any kind. Age/girth are modest for this project's usual bar (a 65-year-old maple, not remotely ancient), and this entry is included specifically because CLAUDE.md's fame test names 'winning or placing highly in a national/European tree-of-the-year contest' as clearing evidence independent of age; the story should lead with the contest history and the distinctive horizontal growth form rather than imply age it does not have. New place, no published city nearby; ships under the 2026-08-31 single-famous-tree exception.

name: Serce Ogrodu (Heart of the Garden)

location.address: Arboretum Wojslawice (University of Wroclaw Botanical Garden branch), Wojslawice, gmina Niemcza, Dzierzoniow County, Lower Silesian Voivodeship, Poland

verified_sources: https://www.wroclaw.pl/zielony-wroclaw/buk-serce-ogrodu-ktory-rosnie-w-arboretum-wojslawice-zostal-drzewem-roku-2023 (fetched directly, quotes Klub Gaja's own 2023 contest results verbatim)
https://www.rmf24.pl/regiony/wroclaw/news-buk-z-wojslawic-europejskim-drzewem-roku,nId,7402100 (fetched directly, headline confirms the European Tree of the Year title)
access: Paid entry. Arboretum Wojslawice is a ticketed botanical garden (a branch of the University of Wroclaw Botanical Garden), open daily 09:00-18:00 in season (mid-April to late October); tickets at the gate or online. The beech stands in the centre of the historic park, a short walk from the entrance.
transport: Wojslawice village, gmina Niemcza, Dzierzoniow County, Lower Silesian Voivodeship; a rural arboretum reached by car, roughly 30km southwest of Wroclaw.
verify_notes: THE STRONGEST FAME EVIDENCE IN THIS WHOLE BATCH, confirmed on two directly-fetched primary sources. Won Poland's national 'Drzewo Roku' (Tree of the Year) 2023 contest outright with 6,643 public votes (wroclaw.pl, quoting Klub Gaja's official results verbatim: 'Buk pospolity "Atropunicea", wiek 200 lat, wys. 14 m, obwod 452 cm', entered by Arboretum Wojslawice - Ogrod Botaniczny Uniwersytetu Wroclawskiego, beating the 2nd-place Malwa & Milosz oak pair in Warsaw and 3rd-place Adam i Ewa oaks in Olsztyn). It then went on to WIN the European Tree of the Year 2024 title outright (rmf24.pl headline, fetched directly: 'Buk z Wojslawic Europejskim Drzewem Roku'), reportedly on over 39,000 votes per a WebSearch summary (not independently fetched, treated as a lead pending a future pass confirming the exact vote count from the European contest's own site, treeoftheyear.org). This is the single strongest, most independently-corroborated fame credential in the entire batch: a national AND continental title, both confirmed on fetched primary sources. SPECIES/GRAFT DETAIL (from the wroclaw.pl article): the tree is a graft, with fast-growing green-leaved common beech (Fagus sylvatica) as rootstock and the slower-growing, red/copper-leaved 'Atropunicea' variety as the scion; leaves change colour through the season (dark purple in spring, rust-green in summer, yellow-orange in autumn), a genuine seasonal-interest tree worth a best_time note for the writer. HISTORY: planted probably at the turn of the 18th/19th century under the von Pritwitz family's ownership of the park; the arboretum itself was created after 1880 when Fritz von Oheimb took over the estate. Named 'Serce Ogrodu' (Heart of the Garden) by the site's current caretakers roughly 30 years before the 2023 article (so approx. early-to-mid 1990s). Widely photographed and painted locally per the source. ALIVE: both sources are from 2023-2024 and describe it as a current, actively cared-for garden centrepiece; no death report. ACCESS: confirmed paid entry, seasonal opening (mid-April to late October per a search result from the arboretum's own site), standard and unremarkable for a botanical garden, satisfies hard rule 10's paid-entry allowance cleanly. Location: Nominatim centroid for the arboretum grounds used as the coordinate (50.71167, 16.86071); the tree's own exact position within the park was not pinned to a primary source this pass, hence approximate rather than confirmed -- a future pass could tighten this from the arboretum's own visitor map. NOTE for a future pass: this is a large, historic botanical garden that almost certainly holds several other individually remarkable specimen trees; this pass only had time to verify the single headline tree. A dedicated Wojslawice/arboretum pass could plausibly build a real multi-tree cluster here rather than leaving it as a lone exception, similar to the Bydgoszcz and Zielona Gora cases recorded elsewhere in this batch. Shipped solo for now under the 2026-08-31 single-famous-tree exception since the fame evidence is unambiguous and does not depend on finding companions.
